page: Amazon Web Services m6i.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual-socket Intel Xeon 8375C processors built on x86_64 architecture. The system exposes 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration consists of 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Networking interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps. The server does not bundle discrete GPUs or local storage disks, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier parallel compute capability, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 87,481.56, Geekbench ray tracing at 99,980.0, and Geekbench image processing at 17,714.0, all placing in the top 10 percent. Multi-threaded evaluations such as stress-ng multi-core (124,975.29) and Geekbench multi-core (17,772.0) place in the top 25 percent. Extended vector operations also test strongly, with PassMark extended instructions reaching 106,991.36 and encryption reaching 112,635.39, supported by hardware AVX-512 and AES instructions. In contrast, single-threaded metrics remain within average margins, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,677.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,909.29.

Data transit metrics show strong throughput across uncached memory scenarios, registering 337.73 GB/sec in read and 133.04 GB/sec in write benchmarks. Serving profiles achieve high performance with static web throughput of 74.45 GB/sec, Redis SET operations reaching 108.92 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations scoring 30,121.63. For machine learning tasks, prompt processing throughput reaches 3,131.97 tokens per second on a 135M model and 196.66 tokens per second on a 7B model, though generative token throughput remains moderate at 22.48 tokens per second on the 7B model.

From an architectural standpoint, the m6i.metal profile provides high resource density on a dedicated bare-metal platform without hypervisor overhead. The omission of local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on network storage for persistence. This hardware configuration is best suited for large-scale enterprise databases, heavy multi-threaded software compilation, high-concurrency container clusters, in-memory caching systems, and non-virtualized enterprise deployments.
